t: Loofah: SVG `<textPath>` and `<mpath>` bypass local-reference restriction
d: Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. Prior to 2.25.3, Loofah's SVG_ALLOW_LOCAL_HREF safelist lists textPath with lowercase spelling that does not match the HTML5 parser's element name and omits mpath, so external href and xlink:href values on those elements survive sanitization. Firefox fetches the attacker-chosen URL when a viewer renders the content, which can disclose the viewer's IP address, user agent, referrer, and access to hosts routable only from the viewer's network. Chrome and WebKit do not fetch these references, and the impact is a network request rather than script execution. The rails-html-sanitizer PermitScrubber reuses the affected safelist when SVG elements are permitted. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

t: datamodel-code-generator < 0.84.0 Code Injection via x-python-type Annotation
d: datamodel-code-generator before 0.84.0 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying a malicious JSON Schema with a crafted x-python-type annotation containing a string ast.Constant node in a subscript slice position, which bypasses validation in parse_python_type_annotation and _python_type_expr_from_ast. Attackers can embed malicious Python expressions such as __import__ calls within quoted string literals in the generated source code, which Pydantic v2 evaluates as a ForwardRef via eval() during model_rebuild(), resulting in arbitrary code execution on developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines, or applications that generate and import the produced models at runtime.

t: Loofah: CSS url() sanitization bypass via escaped parentheses
d: Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. Prior to 2.25.3, Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.scrub_css checks only the first parse of a style attribute, then rebuilds CSS with identifier escapes decoded so escaped parentheses, property names, comments, or quotes can become a live url() without a second safety check. An attacker can use list-style to make a viewer's browser request an attacker-chosen URL when content renders, or cursor to make the request on hover. The request can disclose the viewer's IP address, user agent, access timing, and access to internal-network hosts, but no script survives sanitization and the attacker cannot read the response. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

t: Loofah allowed_uri? treats data:text/html as safe text/plain
d: Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. In 2.25.2, Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? treats a data URI mediatype containing the HTML5 named solidus reference / as malformed and falls back to the allowed text/plain, while a browser decodes the reference and interprets the same value as text/html. An application that validates a user-controlled URL with this helper and renders the approved value in href or another browser-interpreted URI attribute can allow cross-site scripting. Rails::HTML::Sanitizer.allowed_uri? re-exports the affected helper. Loofah's default sanitize() path is not affected because Nokogiri decodes the entity before URI validation. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

t: Sendcloud for WooCommerce 1.0.41 Missing Authorization via AJAX Actions
d: Sendcloud for WooCommerce through 1.0.41 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users, including Subscribers, to access the sc_support_get and sc_support_save AJAX actions due to the absence of capability and nonce checks in SCCSP_Support_Controller. Attackers can call these wp_ajax_ handlers directly or via cross-site request forgery to disclose integration configuration data such as INTEGRATION_ID, SERVICE_POINT, CARRIERS, and MIN_LOG_LEVEL, and to modify the plugin's logging verbosity. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-57760.
r: Sendcloud for WooCommerce: Automated Shipping, Branded Tracking & Returns

t: Image CAPTCHA for Contact Form 7 and WPForms 3.3.29 CAPTCHA Bypass
d: Image CAPTCHA for Contact Form 7 and WPForms through 3.3.29 contains a CAPTCHA bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to defeat the anti-automation control by exploiting a hardcoded static answer in the Contact Form 7 integration. Attackers can submit kc_captcha=kc_human to pass validation in cf7ic_check_if_spam() on every protected form, enabling automated contact-form spam and abuse of actions gated only by this CAPTCHA.
r: Image CAPTCHA for Contact Form 7 and WPForms by HookAndHook (DSGVO/GDPR)

t: Loofah: Regular expression denial of service in the SVG local-reference check
d: Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. Prior to 2.25.3, the Loofah HTML5 sanitizer checks href and xlink:href on elements in SVG_ALLOW_LOCAL_HREF with a regular expression whose line anchor and newline-matching whitespace cause an all-whitespace value to be rescanned from every line start. An attacker can submit an SVG reference element with a long multiline-whitespace attribute and consume CPU quadratically during sanitization. CRuby 3.1 and earlier and JRuby are affected, while CRuby 3.2 and later uses linear-time regular-expression matching. The default safelist reaches the vulnerable check without a configuration change. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

t: Foreman: authorization flaw in the foreman::controller::useraware handling used by api::v2::sshkeyscontroller
d: A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::SshKeysController, where the target user is resolved through Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user using User.find(params[:user_id]) without enforcing the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_ssh_keys permission can exploit this authorization bypass by submitting POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/ssh_keys with another user’s ID and injecting their own public SSH key into the targeted account. The injected key is subsequently propagated to hosts provisioned by that user, potentially allowing the attacker to authenticate to and gain SSH access to the victim’s managed hosts.

t: Foreman: authorization flaw in the mail-notification endpoints implemented by api::v2::mailnotificationscontroller
d: A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::MailNotificationsController, where authorization checks on user-specific mail-notification resources are insufficient. The GET /api/v2/users/:id/mail_notifications endpoint resolves the target account using User.find(params[:id]) without verifying that the authenticated user is authorized to access that user’s notification configuration. Additionally, the POST and PUT /api/v2/users/:user_id/mail_notifications paths call deny_access when the requester is unauthorized but fail to halt execution, allowing the request to continue and persist the unauthorized change despite a 403 response or subsequent DoubleRenderError. This can allow a user to disclose another user’s mail-notification configuration, including mail_query values, and, where write permissions apply, modify or create notification settings for another user.

t: Foreman: authorization flaw in the foreman::controller::useraware#find_user handling used by api::v2::personalaccesstokenscontroller
d: A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user resolves the target account using User.find(params[:user_id]) without applying the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_personal_access_tokens permission can therefore invoke POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/personal_access_tokens with another user’s ID and create a Personal Access Token on their behalf. The resulting plaintext token is returned in the API response, while PersonalAccessToken#check_permissions_after_save only validates create_personal_access_tokens on the token and does not enforce edit_users authorization on the target user. The attacker can then use the forged token to authenticate as the victim, potentially resulting in complete account takeover, including administrator accounts.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Authentication Bypass via users.lua
d: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to set the password of any account flagged must-reset-at-next-login by exploiting missing session validation in the users.lua update_password action. Attackers can reset the password of newly onboarded operator accounts, clearing the password_expiration flag and gaining an immediately usable authenticated foothold on the system. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Unauthenticated Configuration Write via config.lua
d: XWEB EVO 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 contains an unauthenticated arbitrary file write vulnerability that allows remote attackers to modify the system configuration file /etc/xwebconfig.json by sending a crafted POST request to config.lua with action=set, which performs no session validation and writes the raw, unvalidated request body. Attackers can tamper with configuration values such as model and plugin fields or trigger a SYSTEM_NOT_CONFIGURED state via the unauthenticated action=get and action=set operations, resulting in configuration tampering and denial of service. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: BACnet Stack: Stack buffer overflow in Loop internal ReadProperty path via Life_Safety_Zone.accepted-modes on the default BACnet/IP server
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, the current master demo server can be crashed remotely over BACnet/IP by sending a valid Confirmed WriteProperty request that updates loop-1's controlled-variable-reference to point to life-safety-zone-1 / accepted-modes. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

t: Candlepin: consumer certificate can register systems in another organization
d: A missing authorization check has been found in ConsumerResource.setupOwner() function of consumer registration module in the Candlepin package. The registration method checks permission to create a consumer only when the caller is a user. A consumer that authenticates with its identity certificate does not go through that check. A low-privileged network attacker or user who has a valid consumer certificate for one organization can register a new consumer in a different organization by supplying that organization's key. The response includes an identity certificate for the new consumer. With that certificate, the attacker can view the target organization's subscription pools. When the organization is not using simple content access, the attacker can attach that organization's entitlements to the new consumer.

t: Foreman: foreman: api host template render discloses secrets to view_hosts users (incomplete cve-2026-96659 fix)
d: A flaw was found in Foreman. An authenticated user with view_hosts privileges can retrieve rendered provisioning template content for a host via the hosts template API endpoint, disclosing sensitive data such as the host root password. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-96659, which hardened the web UI preview path but left the API host-template render path authorized for Viewer-level users.

t: Rubygem-safemode: safemode: jail allow-list bypass via op-assign expressions
d: A flaw was found in rubygem-safemode. Compound assignment expressions in sandboxed code are evaluated without mediating method calls through the Jail allow-list. An authenticated attacker who can supply template content can invoke arbitrary no-argument methods on objects exposed to the template renderer without Jail mediation, including destructive operations such as host deletion and disclosure of non-allow-listed object state.

t: Rubygem-smart_proxy_dynflow: dynflow console authorizes any client certificate the capsule ca signed
d: An improper authentication vulnerability has been found in the task console in the smart_proxy_dynflow package. The console accepts any client certificate signed by the capsule's certificate authority. It does not check the list of servers the capsule trusts. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already hold such a certificate. They can open the console and read job details. Those details include passwords when a job was given them. They can also cancel a running task.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO OS Command Injection via api.lua
d: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability in the api.lua import_preconfiguration and restore actions, where server_url and related server credential fields are concatenated unescaped into a root curl command executed via io.popen. Attackers can inject malicious shell commands through these unfiltered parameters to achieve arbitrary command execution with root privileges on the underlying system. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: BACnet Stack: Loop reference to long Structured View description causes stack-buffer-overflow
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a stack-buffer-overflow can be triggered in the current master branch when a Loop object reads a referenced property through its default timer path and the referenced property is OBJECT_STRUCTURED_VIEW / PROP_DESCRIPTION containing a long attacker-controlled string. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

t: BACnet Stack: Stack-based buffer overflow in Notification Class RemoveListElement recipient-list decoding
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a RemoveListElement request targeting Notification-Class.recipient-list can trigger a stack-based out-of-bounds write in the current master branch when the request contains more than NC_MAX_RECIPIENTS valid BACnetDestination elements. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

t: BACnet Stack: Stack-based buffer overflow in Notification Class AddListElement recipient-list decoding
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a stack-based out-of-bounds write exists in the Notification Class object implementation when handling AddListElement for the recipient-list property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

t: BACnet Stack: ReinitializeDevice ENDRESTORE can delete existing objects on an empty restore file and still return success
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. In versions 1.5.0 and 1.6.0-rc1, there is a restore logic flaw in bacnet-stack that is reachable through the official, unmodified apps/server management path when BACNET_BACKUP_RESTORE is enabled. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

t: BACnet Stack: Channel member self-reference causes uncontrolled recursion and stack overflow in default BACnet/IP server
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, a remote attacker can trigger an uncontrolled recursion and stack overflow in the default server application of bacnet-stack by abusing the Channel object. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: BACnet Stack: Client-Side Out-of-Bounds Read in AtomicReadFile-ACK Record-Access Handling via RecordCount / fileData[] Mismatch
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, there is a client-side out-of-bounds read in the AtomicReadFile-ACK record-access handling path. The issue is caused by a mismatch between a remote returnedRecordCount value and the fixed local fileData[] array capacity in BACNET_ATOMIC_READ_FILE_DATA. The ACK decode path preserves the remote RecordCount, discards storage for excess records without truncating that count, and a downstream sink later iterates over the original RecordCount and indexes fileData[i] out of bounds. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Hardcoded Administrator Daily Password Authentication Bypass
d: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains a hardcoded credential vulnerability where the Administrator web account is configured to use password_mode daily_password with no stored password, as the Users.authenticate function in lualib_users.lua synthesizes the Administrator configuration without validating any stored secret. Attackers who can derive the MAC-based daily password can authenticate as Administrator to obtain a full admin session on the device. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: BACnet Stack: Uninitialized Value Use in AtomicReadFile-ACK Record-Access Encoder Causes Response Corruption and Conditional Information Disclosure
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.0 to before 1.4.4, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, an uninitialized value use vulnerability in bacnet-stack's AtomicReadFile record-access ACK encoder allows unauthenticated remote attackers to corrupt the encoded OCTET STRING length and payload boundary in network responses by sending a crafted AtomicReadFile request that reaches a successful record-access path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: BACnet Stack: Out-of-Bounds Read in AtomicWriteFile Record Decoder via Unbounded returnedRecordCount
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, an out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in bacnet-stack's AtomicWriteFile record-access path. The bug is caused by a mismatch between an externally controlled returnedRecordCount field and the fixed-size internal fileData[] array used by BACNET_ATOMIC_WRITE_FILE_DATA. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: Governikus AusweisApp Mobile StartPAOSResponse cross site scripting
d: A vulnerability was found in Governikus AusweisApp Mobile up to 2.5.5. This impacts an unknown function of the component StartPAOSResponse Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument ResultMessage results in cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 2.6.0 will fix this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

t: BACnet Stack: NULL pointer dereference in bacnet_device_object_reference_decode() when WriteProperty updates Structured View subordinate-list
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.0 to before 1.4.4, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, a NULL pointer dereference can be triggered in bacnet_device_object_reference_decode() when a WriteProperty request updates OBJECT_STRUCTURED_VIEW / PROP_SUBORDINATE_LIST. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: Atomic-Read-File RecordCount Stack-Based Out-of-Bounds Write in bacnet-stack
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, there is a stack-based out-of-bounds write / stack-buffer-overflow in bacnet-stack when the server processes a malicious Atomic-Read-File request in record access mode. The bug is triggered on the real server side. A crafted request can set an excessively large RecordCount, which is later used as the loop bound for writing record data into a stack-allocated BACNET_ATOMIC_READ_FILE_DATA data structure. However, the stack object only has space for one fileData element. When the loop reaches i = 1, the code computes &data->fileData[1], which is already out of bounds, and the resulting invalid pointer is passed down to memmove(), causing a stack-buffer-overflow. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

t: BACnet Stack: malicious ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK with excessive properties causes global-buffer-overflow in ProcessRPMData()
d: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, in the official apps/epics client tool on v1.6.0-rc1 (not in the generic BACnet RPM ACK decoder alone) a malicious BACnet/IP endpoint can reply to the EPICS tool’s legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request with a syntactically valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK that contains more heading properties than the tool’s fixed local storage can hold. The response is decoded successfully and later consumed by ProcessRPMData(), which writes property values into a fixed global array using an unbounded linear index. This results in a reproducible global-buffer-overflow in apps/epics/main.c. This is a network-reachable memory corruption in the official epics tool’s response-processing path. The root cause is that apps/epics treats a remotely supplied variable-length RPM property list as if it were a trusted, fixed-size local heading-property set. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Information Disclosure via sysinfo.lua
d: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain the device's eth0 MAC address and system clock by accessing sysinfo.lua, which also feeds the pre-login page. Attackers can use the disclosed MAC address and system clock values to offline derive the MAC-based daily password, enabling unauthorized authentication to the device. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Unauthenticated Command Injection via xwconsole.cgi
d: XWEB EVO before 5.6.2 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root by exploiting the setuid-root CGI xwconsole.cgi. Attackers can supply malicious input through the sh parameter, which is passed unsanitized to popen(), to achieve full system compromise. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO OS Command Injection via backup.lua
d: XWEB EVO 5.2.3 through 5.8.8 contains an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root by injecting shell metacharacters into the output device path parameter processed by backup.lua. Attackers can exploit the unescaped concatenation into mount, unzip, and related shell commands run via the wlua interpreter, including through the setuid xwbackup.cgi and xwrestore.cgi interfaces, to achieve full system compromise. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO OS Command Injection via devices.lua
d: XWEB EVO 5.2.3 through 5.8.8 contains an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability in the devices.lua template handling, which allows authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands by injecting unescaped template source into unzip and related shell commands. Attackers can exploit this flaw through the wlua interpreter to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges on the affected device. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Pre-Auth OS Command Injection via Password Field
d: XWEB EVO before 5.6.2 contains a pre-authentication OS command injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands by injecting shell metacharacters into the password field. Attackers can exploit the unescaped interpolation of the password value into the hashpass invocation within login.lua, cleanout.lua, and api.lua to achieve root-level command execution via the setuid wlua interpreter. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Predictable Root Password Generation
d: XWEB EVO through 5.8.8 contains a predictable credential generation vulnerability that allows attackers to derive the Linux root password by computing a fixed prefix combined with a daily password value. Attackers can calculate the deterministic root credential, which before 5.7.0 was identical across all units and from 5.7.0 onward remains derivable from the MAC-based daily password, to gain unauthorized root access to the underlying operating system. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Predictable Administrator Password Generation
d: XWEB EVO 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 contains a weak password generation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to derive the Administrator code-of-the-day password using only the device MAC address and date, with no server secret involved. Attackers can analyze the firmware binary xwpasswd, which itself functions as the password generator, to compute valid Administrator credentials offline and authenticate to the device without authorization. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Hardcoded Administrator Backdoor Password
d: XWEB EVO before 5.6.2 contains a hardcoded backdoor password vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain full administrative access to the built-in Administrator account. Attackers can authenticate using the hardcoded credential xwebevonewgeneration in a single request to obtain a complete admin session and full control over the application. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

t: Algernon: Case-insensitive filesystem lets unauthenticated requests bypass /admin,/repo,/data permission-prefix gate
d: Algernon is a small self-contained pure-Go web server. Prior to version 1.17.10, Algernon's URL-prefix authorization gate matches its protected prefixes (/admin, /repo, /data) with case-sensitive strings.HasPrefix, while the exact same raw req.URL.Path is later resolved against the filesystem. On case-insensitive filesystems (Windows NTFS — always; macOS APFS/HFS+ — default), a request for /Admin/secret.lua evades every protected-prefix check, falls through to the public-prefix accept branch, and then resolves on disk to admin/secret.lua. The result is an unauthenticated bypass of the /admin, /repo, and /data authorization boundary, enabling read (and, for Lua files, execution) of protected content. The permission system is active in the default configuration. This issue has been patched in version 1.17.10.

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB Setuid Lua CGI Root Command Injection
d: XWEB EVO before 5.6.2 contains a command injection vulnerability where the setuid-root Lua CGI interpreter wlua executes system("/usr/bin/lua "+argv) on unsanitized input. Attackers can craft malicious input reached through a .lua CGI endpoint to inject arbitrary commands into the concatenated argv string, achieving command execution with root privileges. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

The Versal™ AI Edge Series Gen 2 Peripheral Protection Unit (XPPU) for the inter-processor interrupt (IPI) buffers does not block unauthorized access as expected. This allows processors in the SoC with any IPI channel access the ability to both read and write to the entire IPI buffer register space as well as the IPI no-buffer register control space.
r: Versal™ AI Edge Series Gen 2 Adaptive SoCs

t: Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO Pre-Auth OS Command Injection via Username
d: XWEB EVO versions 5.2.3 through before 5.7.0 contains a pre-authentication OS command injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands by injecting shell metacharacters into the username field of login.lua, cleanout.lua, or api.lua before the password check occurs. Attackers can exploit this flaw combined with the setuid-root wlua interpreter to execute commands with root privileges, achieving full system compromise. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

Incorrect directory permissions within AMD Vivado™ Lab Solutions could allow a local user-privileged attacker to escalate their privileges, potentially resulting in arbitrary code execution.
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the IOMMU could allow a malicious guest to corrupt hypervisor (HV) pages and potentially cause a host crash leading to loss of availability.

A transient execution vulnerability in some AMD processors may allow an attacker with the ability to execute code on the system to infer data in the L1D cache, potentially resulting in the leakage of sensitive information across privileged boundaries.

Insufficient parameter sanitization in the AMD Secure Processor (ASP) trusted execution environment (TEE) SPDM driver could allow an attacker to supply malicious input, potentially resulting in loss of platform integrity, memory leakage, or denial of service.

t: Yggdrasil-worker-package-manager: yggdrasil-worker-package-manager: path traversal via unsanitized repo name in addrepo/removerepo
d: A flaw was found in yggdrasil-worker-package-manager. An authenticated attacker can exploit this issue to achieve arbitrary file modification or potential privilege escalation. The vulnerability exists because repository management operations fail to sanitize directory traversal sequences (such as '../') within repository names. By supplying a crafted repository name, an attacker can manipulate the root-level worker process into creating or deleting files outside the intended directory, compromising host system integrity.

t: Unverified ownership of the default EMR cluster log location in AWS SDK for pandas
d: Unverified ownership of the default cluster log location in the EMR module in AWS SDK for pandas (awswrangler) from 1.1.0 before 3.18.0 might allow remote actors to read Amazon EMR cluster logs, including job step output, via a pre-created S3 bucket. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 3.18.0 or later. Users who can't upgrade immediately should pass an explicit log location, or create the default EMR log bucket in their own account in each region they use.

t: express-rate-limit skipFailedRequests / skipSuccessfulRequests: with the default MemoryStore, a request from an earlier window is still un-counted from the curr
d: express-rate-limit is a basic rate-limiting middleware for Express. From 8.6.0 until 8.7.2, the built-in MemoryStore returns a Client whose mutable resetTime object is retained by middleware using skipFailedRequests or skipSuccessfulRequests. When a later request resets the client window, MemoryStore.resetClient mutates that same Date, so an earlier request that finishes or disconnects after the reset can pass the stale-window guard and decrement the current window's count. A client able to keep requests in flight across the boundary can obtain a bounded extra burst of up to one additional configured limit in the new window; the behavior does not increase the sustained rate. Stores that return a fresh Date are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 8.7.2.

t: Rust Driver public Client Debug output exposes CSFLE KMS master-key material
d: A MongoDB Rust Driver component that holds client-side field level encryption settings includes key management service credential material in its diagnostic formatting output without redaction. An application that records or displays this formatted output may place that material where a party with read access to the application's diagnostic output can see it, which may result in unintended disclosure of key material.

t: frr: bgpd Send Hold Timer expiry bypasses the FSM, leaving a phantom Established session or crashing bgpd with Graceful Restart
d: In FRRouting 10.1 and later, bgpd does not correctly close a BGP session when the Send Hold Timer (RFC 9687) expires, i.e. when a neighbor has stopped accepting data from the router for twice the hold time. The connection is closed, but bgpd still considers the session to be up. A BGP neighbor that keeps sending KEEPALIVEs but stops reading from its connection, at a time when the router has a large amount of data to send to it (for example while sending it a full routing table), can cause one of the following: * If the neighbor announced Graceful Restart support: bgpd crashes shortly after the session is closed (after the neighbor's announced restart time plus one keepalive interval), taking down all BGP sessions on the router. The neighbor can repeat this each time bgpd restarts. * Otherwise: the session stays stuck in the Established state. The neighbor's routes stay installed and keep being advertised to other peers, and the neighbor cannot reconnect until an operator runs "clear bgp <neighbor>". The neighbor does not need to be malicious; an overloaded or stuck peer can trigger the same behavior. Required configuration: no special configuration is needed. Any BGP neighbor with an established session can trigger the issue under default settings, for example: router bgp 65001 neighbor 192.0.2.2 remote-as 65002 Graceful Restart helper mode, which leads to the crash, is enabled by default. With default timers (keepalive 60s, hold time 180s), the session is closed about 6 minutes after the neighbor stops reading.

t: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - IDOR allowing restricted file downloads in jDownloads < 4.1.8
d: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - IDOR allowing restricted file downloads in jDownloads < 4.1.8 - The `other_file_id` parameter could reference another download’s file without fully enforcing the target download’s access restrictions. This allowed files to be delivered to users who were not authorised to access the target download.

t: Loofah: Mutation XSS in the HTML5 scrubbers through unescaped attribute values
d: Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. From 2.21.0 until 2.25.3, Loofah's HTML5 APIs Loofah.html5_fragment, Loofah.html5_document, and the scrub_html5_* methods can emit sanitized output that a browser reparses as different markup when used with Nokogiri before 1.19.5, because those Nokogiri versions do not escape angle brackets in attribute values. MathML can place markup inside an allowed attribute so the reparsed output becomes live HTML. The :strip scrubber is affected in every browser, while :prune and :escape are affected in WebKit browsers. Loofah's HTML4 APIs, Loofah::Helpers.sanitize, :whitewash, rails-html-sanitizer's default configuration, and JRuby are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

t: OpenNMS reflected cross-site scripting in the web UI via request parameters
d: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in the web user interface of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. Several web UI pages copy request parameter values into the HTML response without correct contextual output encoding. A remote attacker can craft a link that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the OpenNMS origin when an authenticated user opens it. The script runs in the victim's browser with the victim's session, so the attacker can read page data and send same-origin requests as the victim. The fix encodes the affected request values. On pages that use AngularJS, the fix also stops client-side template evaluation of the reflected values. The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

t: Symfony: The "private_ranges" Trusted Proxies Shortcut Trusts Clients Presenting an IPv4-Mapped, 6to4, Teredo or NAT64 Address as Reverse Proxies
d: The Symfony FrameworkBundle framework.trusted_proxies option and the HttpFoundation Request::setTrustedProxies() method trust remote clients as reverse proxies when the private_ranges shortcut is used, allowing remote attackers to spoof the client IP address, host and scheme in Symfony FrameworkBundle versions 7.1 prior to 7.4.23 and 8.x prior to 8.1.11, and HttpFoundation versions 7.2 prior to 7.4.23 and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. The private_ranges and PRIVATE_SUBNETS keywords resolved to IpUtils::PRIVATE_SUBNETS, the deny list of NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient, which lists the private and special-purpose prefixes a server must not connect to. Since the fix for CVE-2026-48736 (7.4.13 and 8.0.13), this list also covers the IPv6 prefixes that embed an IPv4 address: IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), IPv4-compatible (::/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), Teredo (2001::/32) and NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96). The IPv4-mapped entry has been in the list since the private_ranges shortcut was introduced, in 7.1 for framework.trusted_proxies and in 7.2 for Request::setTrustedProxies(). Over-blocking is safe for a deny list, but when the same entries are used as the allow list of trusted proxies, they trust remote clients. A client whose connection arrives with such a source address is treated as a reverse proxy, and the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Port and X-Forwarded-Prefix headers it sends are honoured. For example, with Request::setTrustedProxies(['private_ranges'], ...), a request with REMOTE_ADDR set to ::ffff:203.0.113.7 and the headers X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.9, X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example.com and X-Forwarded-Proto: https makes getClientIp() return 10.0.0.9, getHost() return evil.example.com and isSecure() return true. Two kinds of deployments are exposed: a server listening on the IPv6 wildcard address without IPV6_V6ONLY reports every IPv4 client in the IPv4-mapped form, so every client is trusted, and a server reachable over IPv6 trusts any client sourcing from 6to4 or Teredo space, which is globally routed, whatever its listener. A spoofed client address defeats IP allow lists, rate limiting and audit logs; a spoofed host poisons the URLs written into password reset and login link e-mails and into shared caches; a spoofed scheme satisfies requires_channel: https over plain HTTP. Symfony 6.4 does not point any trusted proxy setting at IpUtils::PRIVATE_SUBNETS and is not affected by default, but an application that passes that constant to Request::setTrustedProxies() itself could be exposed in the same way on any version. This issue is fixed in 7.4.23 and 8.1.11.

t: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - Authenticated path traversal in jDownloads < 4.1.8
d: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - Authenticated path traversal in jDownloads < 4.1.8 - A manipulated `update_file` form parameter could bypass the intended server-file selection restrictions and move files from outside the permitted selection directory or assign them to a download. This could expose file contents and remove source files from their original locations.

t: OpenNMS argument injection in ad-hoc RRD graphs
d: An argument injection vulnerability exists in the ad-hoc RRD graph feature of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. The ad-hoc graph endpoint (GET /graph/graph.png?adhoc=true) copies request parameters into the rrdtool command line without validation. A low-privileged authenticated user (ROLE_USER or ROLE_DASHBOARD) can insert extra rrdtool arguments. An injected --daemon argument makes the server connect to an attacker-chosen address, which is a server-side request forgery. An injected DEF statement reads a local RRD file by absolute path. The command runs through exec with an argument array and no shell, so arbitrary operating system command execution is not possible. The fix validates the ad-hoc graph parameters against allowlists. The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

d: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Subscriber identity not bound to the record acted upon in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - An authenticated user of any privilege level can subscribe or unsubscribe any other subscriber to or from any mailing list of the site.

d: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - Publishing of files without approval in jDownloads < 4.1.8 - Manipulated frontend submission parameters could bypass the intended publication and ownership rules. d: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - SSRF via external download URL field jDownloads < 4.1.8 - HTTP redirects when retrieving external download URLs could bypass validation of the original destination. t: Sssd: sssd: null pointer dereference in pam responder when protocol version negotiation is skipped
d: A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder. A local attacker can send an authentication request without first negotiating the client protocol version. The responder dereferences a NULL protocol-version pointer and crashes, disrupting SSSD-backed authentication. Repeated crafted requests can sustain the denial of service.

t: Sssd: sssd: local denial of service through unchecked oauth2 json code type in pam responder
d: A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder on builds with the JSON PAM extension enabled. A local attacker can submit a crafted authentication request containing a non-string OAuth2 code value. Missing JSON type validation leads to a NULL pointer dereference, terminating the PAM responder and disrupting SSSD-backed authentication.

t: Sssd: sssd: stack buffer overflow during rsa certificate-to-ssh key conversion
d: A flaw was found in SSSD's conversion of X.509 certificate RSA public keys to SSH keys. Missing size checks before copying RSA components into fixed-size stack buffers can cause a stack buffer overflow. An attacker able to supply a certificate with oversized RSA components that passes the configured certificate checks can cause denial of service and corrupt SSH responder memory.

d: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in AcyMailing 6.0.0 - 11.1.1 - Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in AcyMailing 6.0.0 through 11.1.1. Holding that key, the attacker can act as that subscriber on those endpoints, which includes triggering the GDPR data export and the GDPR account deletion where those options are enabled.
